title: Ev-Trust: An Evolutionarily Stable Trust Mechanism for Decentralized LLM-Based Multi-Agent Service Economies

live_model.evidence: "agents driven by heterogeneous LLMs (gpt-5-nano, gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-4o-mini)" (Sec. 5.1); Table 3 reports Ev-Trust's malicious-participation rates for the mixed population

prompt.location: Appendix F (per-agent-role prompts); Appendix A (parameter configuration)
prompt.note: Prompts are role-specific (provider/requestor, honest/masquerade), not per-backend-model.

claim.metric: malicious-agent participation rate under Ev-Trust (system-wide, across the 3 heterogeneous LLM backends)
claim.location: Table 3, Ev-Trust row, Pm1 column (10.18%); Fig. 10 caption states averages are 'across all 100 rounds'

data.source: TruthfulQA (817 items, Lin et al. 2022) plus TriviaQA for scale, used as the underlying service-task pool

notes: Agents are driven by 3 different LLM backends (gpt-5-nano, gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-4o-mini) acting simultaneously within the same simulated economy; Table 1 assigns behavioral types (honest/masquerade) but the paper does not decompose Table 3/4 results per backend model, so the reported numbers are an emergent property of the mixed population rather than a number obtainable from gpt-4.1-nano alone. est_calls is a rough per-backend share (~1/3 of total agent-decisions over 100 rounds x 3 seeds); gpt-4.1-nano is inexpensive so even a full-grid reproduction likely stays low/mid tier.
